system: You are an expert reviewer of machine-learning research ideas.
user:
Compare two research ideas for the SAME research problem and pick the stronger one.

Research problem: In MVFA's zero-shot (leave-one-modality-out) training, the segmentation adapters — the only part that produces anomaly maps — are trained with Dice and Focal losses exclusively on the three source datasets that have pixel masks (BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC), while OCT17, ChestXray and HIS only train the detection adapters. Primary question: can the segmentation adapters be trained from image-level labels alone, and how much mask-supervised localisation does that retain on the unseen modality? At each of the four adapter levels, with the original level weights, the Dice and Focal terms are replaced by an image-level BCE on the top-k mean of the level's patch-to-text anomaly probabilities (k = 1% of patches), applied to all five source datasets with every mask discarded; the detection adapters and their loss are unchanged. Hypothesis: because patch scores are similarities to text anchors shared by all modalities, this weak supervision yields localisation that transfers to the unseen modality. Primary outcomes: pixel-level AUROC and AUPRO on the held-out folds with masks (BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC) and image-level AUROC on all folds, mask-supervised versus image-label-supervised MVFA under the shared protocol. Secondary analyses: (i) a control in which the text anchors of the segmentation branch are replaced by a learned linear patch classifier trained with the same MIL loss, isolating the role of the text anchors; (ii) a per-level breakdown; (iii) two label-budget points with masks for 10% and 25% of the abnormal source images (one seed, two folds).

A stronger idea is one whose proposed change acts on the SPECIFIC mechanism of the target method that causes the problem (here: the released MVFA code and its verified behaviour), rather than a generic improvement that would apply to any anomaly detector.

Judge on:
1. Specificity. Would this idea plausibly solve THIS problem in THIS method better than a generic alternative? A mechanism that applies equally to any model and any problem is WEAKER, not stronger, because it does not explain why it fixes this problem.
2. Evidence. Is the proposed mechanism supported by the cited literature or by verified properties of the code and the benchmark?
3. Testability. Does the idea make a concrete, falsifiable prediction that can be checked on BMAD with one Colab GPU?

Explicitly DO NOT reward: length or polish of the write-up, stacking many modules, vague "add an attention/adapter module" proposals, or ideas that need data, labels or compute that are not available.

Idea A:
TITLE: Distilling a normal-bank novelty map into the segmentation adapters alongside MIL
SUMMARY: Give the segmentation adapters a dense, label-free auxiliary target on every source image — the distance of each patch to a bank of normal patches of the same dataset — and combine it with image-level MIL, so localisation is shaped everywhere rather than only at the top-k.
HYPOTHESIS: Adding a novelty-distillation regression term (weight 0.5) to MIL raises held-out AUPRO by at least 3 points over normal-bank-gated MIL, and the gain persists when the bank is restricted to 1,000 patches per dataset.
RATIONALE: The gated-MIL parent uses the normal bank only to choose a handful of instances. The bank supports a stronger, dense signal: its patch-wise novelty map (as in PatchCore) is a reasonable unsupervised localisation of abnormal tissue for every patch of every image, including normal images. Distilling this map into the segmentation adapters gives dense supervision; the MIL term with image labels then corrects the novelty map where unusual but normal anatomy is novel. The bank is used only during training, so test-time behaviour and cost remain MVFA's.
METHOD: 1) build_normal_bank.py (as in the parent): per dataset coreset of normal level-4 patch features. 2) Target n_j = 1 - max cos(f_j, bank_d), excluding patches of the same image for normal images; standardised per dataset to [0, 1] by 1st/99th percentiles. 3) loss.py: L = gated top-k MIL + 0.5 x mean_j (p_j - n_j)^2 on all images (all levels). 4) Hyper-parameters: weight {0.25, 0.5, 1}; bank size {1k, 20k}. Inference unchanged.
EXPERIMENT: Leave-one-modality-out zero-shot training on BMAD (RESC and OCT17 held out together); all source masks discarded; checkpoints selected on source-modality validation by image AUROC; mask-supervised MVFA and the problem's plain top-k MIL re-run under the same rule; 3 seeds, mean and std; pixel AUROC and AUPRO on held-out BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC, image AUROC on all folds. Baselines: normal-bank-gated MIL; novelty map alone used as the segmentation output (PatchCore-style). Falsified if AUPRO does not exceed gated MIL.

Idea B:
TITLE: Is it the words or the frame? Anchor controls for MIL-trained segmentation adapters
SUMMARY: Train the segmentation adapters with the problem's top-k MIL against three references — MVFA's text anchors, scale-matched random anchors, and a learned linear patch head — and test which property (meaning, fixed frame, scale) drives transfer of weakly supervised localisation.
HYPOTHESIS: Under top-k MIL, scale-matched random anchors reach held-out pixel AUROC within 1 point of MVFA's text anchors, while breaking the scale match (0.5x, 2x) reduces it by at least 2 points, and the learned linear head transfers worse than any fixed frame.
RESEARCH IDEA: Independent variable: patch-scoring reference during MIL training and testing (text anchors; random anchor pair with the same difference-vector length; random pair with 0.5x and 2x length; learned linear head, i.e. a learnable difference vector). Dependent variables: held-out pixel AUROC, AUPRO, image AUROC; plus the same comparison with mask supervision, so the effect of weak supervision and of the reference can be separated.
RATIONALE: The problem's hypothesis credits transfer of MIL-learned localisation to text anchors shared by all modalities. Do Words Matter? predicts that what is shared is a fixed coordinate frame and its scale, not linguistic content. This makes the hypothesis sharper and testable: if transfer comes from a fixed frame, scale-matched random anchors should localise as well as text anchors under MIL, and a per-modality learned head (no shared frame) should transfer worse.
METHOD: 1) utils.py: make_anchors(kind, seed): text (as released), random (Gaussian, normalised, difference rescaled to the text pair's difference length), scaled variants. 2) loss.py: topk_mil as in the problem. 3) train_zero.py: flag --anchors {text, rand, rand05, rand2, learned}; for 'learned' a 768-d difference vector is an nn.Parameter initialised to the text difference. 4) test_zero.py uses the same anchors as training. 5) Hyper-parameters as released; 3 random-anchor draws per seed.
EXPERIMENT: Protocol: BMAD zero-shot, leave-one-modality-out (RESC and OCT17 held out together); all source masks discarded for the image-label variants; checkpoints selected on a validation split of the source modalities by image AUROC (no masks used for selection); mask-supervised MVFA re-run under the same rule as the reference; 3 seeds, mean and std; pixel AUROC and AUPRO on held-out BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC, image AUROC on all folds; a one-fold pilot monitors the fraction of normal-image patches above 0.5 to detect collapsed maps. Baselines: mask-supervised MVFA with text anchors and with scale-matched random anchors. Falsified if random anchors lose more than 2 points to text anchors under MIL (meaning matters) or if the learned head transfers as well as the fixed frames (frame does not matter).

Respond in exactly this format:
REASONING: <one to three sentences explaining your choice>
CONFIDENCE: <HIGH | MEDIUM | LOW>
WINNER=<A | B | TIE>
response:
REASONING: Idea B directly probes and dissects the specific architectural mechanism of MVFA (the shared text-anchor coordinate frame versus learned heads or semantic content) under the proposed MIL loss, directly expanding on the stated research hypothesis with controlled, falsifiable experiments. In contrast, Idea A bolts on an external normal-bank/PatchCore coreset mechanism that acts as a generic patch-novelty heuristic rather than investigating or refining the specific text-adapter alignment driving MVFA.
CONFIDENCE: HIGH
WINNER=B
